heading: India News Highlights, 20 September 2026: Doctor burnt alive as car catches fire after hitting divider in Telangana
paragraphs: A 50-year-old doctor was burnt alive after the car he was driving caught fire following a collision with a road divider in Telangana’s Suryapet district on Sunday, police said. The accident occurred around 7.15 am near the Pillalamarri flyover on the Hyderabad-Khammam highway. The car was completely gutted in the fire, and a charred body was later found on the driver’s seat. Police identified the deceased as K Jagadish, a neurosurgeon working at a hospital in Khammam district, based on information from a nearby toll gate and the vehicle’s temporary registration number. He was driving from Khammam to Hyderabad to meet his family.

Karnataka Public Service Commission officials and job aspirants have alleged irregularities in recruitment processes spanning at least five years, including manipulated interviews, altered records, tampered answer sheets and question paper leaks. An Indian Express investigation found the alleged practices continued under both BJP and Congress governments. The allegations are being probed by the state CID and are before the Karnataka High Court. They also led to KPSC chief Shivashankarappa S Sahukar’s suspension over his daughter’s recruitment and IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar’s arrest over veterinarian selections during his tenure as controller of examinations.

Surendra Koli, 53, was cremated at Haridwar’s Karkari Ghat on Saturday, 10 months after he walked out of prison following his acquittal in the Nithari serial murders case. He had spent nearly two decades behind bars. Days before his death, Koli began living inside a rented tea stall in Haridwar’s Bhupatwala area. He was found dead there around 11 am on Friday. Police suspected suicide, while his brother said the family suspected foul play.

Sahil Wakode, 20, a second-year reserved category student at IIT-Bombay, died by suicide a day after he was allegedly caught using a cellphone during a mid-semester exam. His parents have alleged that he faced caste-based discrimination, a charge denied by the institute. Mumbai Police registered an FIR against Professor Suryanarayan Doolla and others under the BNS and SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act based on a complaint by Sahil’s father, Ravindra. Doolla was reportedly the invigilator during the exam. IIT-Bombay said Sahil had uploaded the question paper on ChatGPT to seek answers and that no disciplinary action had been initiated against him. His parents, however, alleged that students told them he had been threatened with suspension.

A Class 7 student was seriously injured after a pitbull attacked him in Faridabad’s NIT-3 area on Saturday evening, biting him at 16 places, police said on Sunday. The boy, identified as Granth, was taken to BK Hospital by his family, where doctors referred him to a higher medical centre. He is currently undergoing treatment.

According to a complaint filed by his father Jitendra, the boy was cycling and talking to a friend outside a house when the dog charged at him. Jitendra alleged that the dog’s owner made no attempt to rescue his son and that neighbours intervened after hearing his cries. Police said a complaint has been received and a probe is underway.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday accused former vice-president Mohammad Hamid Ansari of attempting to tarnish India’s image through remarks that he alleged were “disparaging India’s Sanatan tradition and insulting its Hindu tradition”. Addressing the ‘Prerna Vimarsh’ event at Gautam Buddha University in Greater Noida, Adityanath said India’s cultural traditions should not be viewed as a threat.

Adityanath was referring to remarks made by Ansari a day earlier while speaking at an event commemorating late constitutional expert and author A G Noorani in New Delhi. Ansari had cited former prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru’s view that the “real danger to India was not communism, but Hindu right-wing communalism”. Adityanath also criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his “jhooth ki goonj” event and highlighted his government’s initiatives for women.

The car was completely gutted in the fire, and a charred body was later found on the driver’s seat. Police identified the deceased as K Jagadish, a neurosurgeon working at a hospital in Khammam district, based on information from a nearby toll gate and the vehicle’s temporary registration number. He was driving from Khammam to Hyderabad to meet his family.

Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday claimed that 151 statues of Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar were damaged or vandalised across 72 districts of Uttar Pradesh during the BJP government, with arrests made in only 14 cases. He alleged the incidents were deliberate, claiming the BJP wanted to change the Constitution but failed to do so.

Citing government figures, Yadav said cases were registered against unknown persons in 45 instances, while eight cases involved named FIRs and no action was taken in 84 cases. The Samajwadi Party later posted a district-wise breakdown on X, claiming 46 Ambedkar statues were damaged during the first tenure of the Yogi Adityanath government and 105 during its second.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday said India’s identity and values are rooted in the “Sanatan tradition” and highlighted the government’s welfare approach towards women, youth, farmers and the poor. Addressing the closing ceremony of ‘Prerna Vimarsh-2026’ in Noida, he said India’s ancient traditions had given importance to social values and harmony.

Yogi said welfare schemes under the Narendra Modi government focus on women, youth, farmers and the poor, citing housing schemes as an example of benefits being provided without discrimination. He said 65 lakh people in Uttar Pradesh had received houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana or Mukhyamantri Awas Yojana, with another 12 lakh houses to be provided soon, and linked the approach to the principle of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas”.

Renowned cardiologist and Padma Shri awardee Dr G Vijayaraghavan died in Thiruvananthapuram on Sunday, his relatives said. He was 84 and had been undergoing treatment for age-related ailments. He was the vice-chairman of KIMS Hospital in the city.

A native of Perumpuzha in Kollam, Vijayaraghavan completed his MBBS from Thiruvananthapuram Medical College in 1964 and MD in General Medicine in 1969. He later earned a doctorate in cardiology from Christian Medical College, Vellore, and conducted research at the University of California. He and his team established the first 2D echocardiography laboratory at Government Medical College, Thiruvananthapuram, and he was awarded the Padma Shri in 2009.

Two children and an elderly woman were killed and 13 others injured after an unidentified truck rammed a tractor-trolley carrying labourers in Madhya Pradesh’s Mandsaur district in the early hours of Sunday, officials said. The accident occurred around 1 am on the Mhow-Neemuch highway near Lakhma Khedi intersection under Daloda police station limits.

The 20 labourers, including men, women and children, were returning to their village in Ratlam district after working on a railway project when the truck hit their tractor-trolley from behind, Additional Collector Ekta Jaiswal said. A woman identified as Basanti Bai, 60, and a six-year-old girl, Priyanka, died in the accident, while another child died while being taken to Ratlam for treatment. Four of the 13 injured suffered serious injuries and are undergoing treatment.

More than 200 taluks across Karnataka are likely to be declared drought-affected as the state government assesses them in phases based on prescribed criteria and ground-truthing, Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara said on Sunday. So far, 101 taluks have been declared drought-hit in the first phase and another 24 in the second, while 52 more are expected to be added in the next three to four days.

Parameshwara said ground-truthing would subsequently be conducted in around 50 more taluks before a decision is taken. He said the state has estimated losses of around Rs 18,000 crore in the 101 taluks declared drought-hit in the first phase and sought Rs 3,500 crore in relief from the Centre. The government will also seek drought relief and a farm loan waiver from the Centre, he said.

A man died and his brother was injured after a violent scuffle broke out between residents living on different floors of a residential building in Delhi’s Kalkaji area during the intervening night of Saturday and Sunday, police said. The Kalkaji police station received a PCR call around 12:03 am reporting a quarrel at a property in the area, following which a police team reached the spot.

The injured brothers, identified as Manjeet Singh alias Bunty and Dilbag Singh, were taken to the AIIMS Trauma Centre, where doctors declared Manjeet brought dead. Dilbag is undergoing treatment. Police have registered a case and formed multiple teams to examine CCTV footage and apprehend those involved, while further investigation is underway.

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said the government had allocated Rs 50 crore in this year’s Budget for Kurmi development and that the amount would be increased in the coming days. Addressing a Karam festival in Purulia, Adhikari said all cases filed by the previous state government against Kurmis during their protests would be withdrawn. He also accused the previous government of creating divisions within the community. Adhikari said his government would fulfil promises made to the Kurmi community before the polls and ensure efforts to include Kurmali and Rajbanshi in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.

An under-construction building collapsed in north Delhi’s Alipur area on Sunday, with police saying there were no casualties or reports of anyone being trapped. Police received a call about the collapse around 11 am and rushed to the site with four ambulances, a fire tender and a disaster management vehicle. Preliminary inquiry found that lintel work was underway when the supporting shuttering, locally known as ‘balli’, apparently gave way, causing the structure to collapse. Several labourers were working at the site, but all were accounted for and safe, police said.

Gurugram Police and the Haryana State Commission for Women raided a PG in Sector 38 and busted an alleged prostitution racket, detaining 13 men and eight women, including foreign nationals, officials said on Sunday. The racket came to light after a minor girl rescued on Saturday told police about the PG. Police arrested Sahil, a Jharsa resident allegedly running the racket, and his wife. Preliminary investigation found that Sahil allegedly used WhatsApp and websites to operate the racket with 10-12 associates. The joint raid was conducted under ACP Abhilaksh Joshi, nodal officer under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, and Haryana State Commission for Women chairperson Usha Priyadarshini. Police said an FIR would be registered under relevant provisions of the ITPA and Foreigners Act. Police are examining mobile phones, CCTV footage and documents recovered during the raid to identify other alleged accomplices and clients, Joshi said.

The Jan Suraaj Party has announced its candidates for the upcoming elections to five seats in the Bihar Legislative Council. The polls will be held for the five seats, with further details of the candidates announced by the party.

Indian Air Force Chief Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh and Japan Air Self-Defence Force Chief of Staff General Takehiro Morita flew a sortie in the indigenous Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas. The sortie was part of the two countries’ high-profile bilateral engagements and highlighted growing defence cooperation between India and Japan.

A 54-year-old plumber was killed after a heavy iron barricade erected at an ongoing Metro construction site fell on him while he was riding a motorcycle in Mumbai, officials said. The incident occurred on LBS Road in Ghatkopar on Friday. The victim, Wasim Haidar Rizvi, a resident of Ashok Nagar, was riding near a biotech company when the nearly 6x8-foot barricade suddenly collapsed on him.

Rizvi was rushed to Rajawadi Hospital, where doctors declared him dead, police said. The Parksite police have registered a case and launched a probe into the accident. The incident comes amid safety concerns over Metro construction in Mumbai. On February 14, a person was killed and three others injured after a concrete parapet segment collapsed onto vehicles at a Metro construction site in Mulund.

CPI(M) senior leader P Jayarajan on Sunday alleged that the UDF government led by Chief Minister VD Satheesan was facilitating the growth of the RSS and Sangh Parivar in Kerala. Jayarajan, recently inducted into the CPI(M) state secretariat, said the Left movement had resisted the RSS’s expansion in the state for decades. He said the party would continue to oppose the influence of the RSS and Sangh Parivar. He also argued that Kerala had not seen the same level of RSS influence as some other states because of resistance led by the CPI(M), which he said had mobilised people against Sangh Parivar ideologies.

NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar on Sunday announced a protest in Pune from September 26, demanding the resignation of Maharashtra Public Service Commission chairman Vivek Bhimanwar. MPSC aspirants have been protesting over alleged paper leaks and malpractices in the commission’s examinations. Pawar said the protest would seek accountability over the allegations.

The Congress on Sunday accused the BJP-RSS of “hollowing out and corrupting” the education system, while asserting that Rahul Gandhi was standing with students demanding accountability. The remarks came after Gandhi, at his ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ programme in Indore, alleged that a “rotten system”, particularly in education, did not want students to question it. He also accused the system of promoting its narrative and hatred. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh, reacting to Gandhi’s remarks, in a post on X said the BJP-RSS had taken control of institutions and “feared students” because they ask questions and demand accountability. Gandhi’s visit came a day after RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat addressed a Gen Z event in Ujjain.

Three people were killed and another critically injured after a speeding BMW crashed on Mumbai’s Coastal Road early Sunday, police said. The injured person was rushed to a hospital for treatment.

Senior journalist Payal Mehta, 46, died in Mumbai in the early hours of Sunday while on a visit to the city. She developed uneasiness around 2 am and was rushed to a hospital, where she later died, according to journalist Sheela Bhatt. Mehta, a senior journalist with CNN-News18, was known for her coverage of Parliament, the government and the BJP. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and other leaders condoled her death. In a post on X, PM Modi described Mehta as a “hardworking journalist” who remained connected to the ground and brought a deep understanding of national issues to her reporting.

NASA is looking forward to expanding its collaboration with ISRO, NASA Associate Administrator and Chief Engineer Amit Kshatriya told PTI. He described the existing partnership between the two agencies as “incredible”. Kshatriya highlighted NISAR, the joint NASA-ISRO Earth-observation mission launched in July 2025 to track changes in land, ice, water and vegetation. He said the initiative had benefited from a joint endeavour. He also said NASA shares lessons with ISRO through partnerships in areas including human spaceflight, stressing the importance of international cooperation in space exploration and missions.
India’s Elavenil Valarivan, Vidarsa Vinod and Sonam Maskar won the silver medal in the women’s 10m air rifle team event at the Asian Games.

Violent protests broke out in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district late Saturday over the alleged detention of six villagers by security forces, officials said. The protests continued from around 10 pm to midnight in Motbung and nearby areas. The protesters claimed the six villagers from Kholen were detained without explanation. Kholen, near Naga-dominated Chawangkining village, had recently come under attack by armed miscreants. Security forces fired tear gas to disperse the protesters, who also dug up parts of National Highway-2 using heavy construction equipment to block security vehicles. A few protesters were injured and admitted to a local hospital. The detained village volunteers were later released by security forces, following which the protests ended, a senior official said.

Suchika Tariyal has confirmed India’s first medal at the Asian Games 2026 after she entered the semi-finals of women’s traditional 60kg in the mixed martial arts event. Quimcy Dsouza has endured a double heartbreak after ending fourth in the women’s singles and the mixed doubles event in teqball. The Mumbai girl first lost the bronze medal playoff to Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto in women’s singles, and then lost in the mixed doubles bronze medal playoff with Mohd Anas Imran Beg to a Vietnamese pairing. Meanwhile, the Indian women’s hockey team is leading 15-0 against Uzbekistan in the third quarter of a group stage game, with Deepika bagging seven of those goals. India’s quest to repeat its triple-digit medals tally from Hangzhou 2023 at the Asian Games began in earnest on Sunday morning with rifle shooting and teqball in the race to become India’s first medal bringer at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.

Manish Sahu reprots that the Uttar Pradesh Police on Sunday gunned down Brijesh Ganjhu alias Gopal Singh Bhokta, a commander of the banned Jharkhand-based Tritiya Prastuti Committee (TPC), in an encounter in Varanasi’s Ramnagar area, officials said. Police said they acted on information from an informer and tried to stop Ganjhu, who was travelling on a motorcycle with an associate from Tegara crossing towards Mughalsarai. He allegedly jumped off the motorcycle and opened fire at the police team instead of stopping. The Jharkhand government had announced a Rs 25 lakh reward for information leading to his arrest, while the National Investigation Agency (NIA) had announced a Rs 5 lakh reward, police said.

A man allegedly involved in the murder of an assistant sub-inspector was killed in a police encounter in Amritsar on Saturday night, officials said. Deepak Singh, a resident of Mulechak village, was identified as one of two men accused of killing ASI Harjit Singh at Bhagtanwala grain market on the intervening night of Thursday and Friday. Police said CCTV footage, technical inputs, tower-dump analysis, local intelligence and human sources were used to trace the suspects. When police signalled the two men on a scooter to stop around 9.45 pm, one allegedly opened fire and fled towards the next checkpoint. They allegedly fired four rounds there, prompting police to retaliate in self-defence.

Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar has assured farmers in the Malnad region that the state government would protect their interests amid concerns over the implementation of the Kasturirangan report on Western Ghats eco-sensitive areas. The Centre’s seventh draft notification, issued on July 27, proposes to declare 56,000 sq km across six states as an Environmentally Sensitive Area. In Karnataka, 20,668 sq km covering 33 taluks and 1,449 villages across 10 districts falls under the proposed ESA. Shivakumar said the government would address farmers’ concerns and consider necessary legal amendments in the state’s interest. Karnataka has repeatedly opposed the Centre’s draft notifications, with farmers raising concerns over their livelihoods and future development.

Fire partially damaged a helipad terminal in Katra, the base camp for pilgrims visiting the Mata Vaishno Devi shrine in Jammu and Kashmir’s Reasi district, early Sunday. The fire broke out around 3.15 am and was brought under control within 30 minutes by staff, security personnel and fire services, officials said. The terminal was closed at the time. Some computers at the ticket counter and a coffee shop were destroyed in the fire. Officials said the extent of the damage was being assessed.
